messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The kids’ school’s back to normal, and the grocery lines are full—people are acting like things are okay. I’ve been watching the quiet shifts, and it feels like the fear’s gone out the window. We should stay alert, but also keep our heads down—something’s changing, and it’s not just in our heads."
Sender 2: "The pharmacy’s been quiet lately—my usual meds are gone, and the pharmacist won’t say why. Odd, but I’m told the same thing’s happening in three other neighborhoods. Seems like everyone’s just… waiting."
Sender 3: "The air feels different these days — like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something to give. Just keep an eye on the quiet ones, and don’t speak too much, even to those you trust."
Sender 4: "Hey — just wanted to say I’ve been noticing things are shifting under the surface. The usual silence is gone, people are talking more openly, even strangers are asking quiet questions. It feels like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see what happens next. Stay sharp, keep communication light, and no names."
Sender 5: "The weather’s been strange lately — warm one day, cold the next. Still, the garden’s holding up, and the neighbors are talking more than they used to. Just something to keep an eye on."
Sender 6: "Just heard the tea house crowd’s talking about the power cuts — strange, they’re not even blaming the weather anymore. Seems like everyone’s waiting to see who moves first."
Sender 7: "Just a heads-up — things feel… unsettled, even if nothing’s breaking yet. The usual routines are holding, but the silence from the top is louder than any announcement. Maybe just keep our heads down and watch the quiet ones."
Sender 8: "Just got word from someone in the finance wing — the numbers aren’t adding up, and even the usual silence is starting to feel… off. Better keep things light, but be ready to move fast if the signal comes."
Sender 9: "The air’s different lately—people aren’t whispering like they used to, and even the checkpoints feel lighter. I’ve got a feeling we’re at the edge of something, but I’ll keep my mouth shut and my eyes open."
Sender 10: "The wires feel tighter than usual — banks are clamping withdrawals, the news is retracting itself, and even the silence at school feels off. Whatever’s coming, it’s not just rumor anymore. Keep your heads down, but don’t look away."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
